html: The Mangala are an Aboriginal Australian people of the northern Great Sandy Desert in Western Australia, south of the Fitzroy River. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. Their neighbours were the Karajarri to the west, the Nyikina to the north, the Walmajarri to the east and the Yulparija to the south. Like the Walmajarri, many Mangala families moved north out of the desert in the 20th century to cattle stations and mission settlements along the Fitzroy valley and the coast.
